source.verbatim_statement: For any constant $\gamma\in\left({1}/{2},1\right)$ and estimators $\hat{m}(x)$ and $\hat{g}(d,x)$ that satisfy Assumption \ref{asmp:estimator-bounded}, for any given weight function $w$, the minimax risk of estimating the \textsc{WATE} is $\mathfrak{M}_{n,\gamma}^{\wate}\left(\gF_{e_n,e_n',f_n}\right) = \Omega\left( \max\{e_n,e_n'\} f_n\cdot\Vert w\Vert _{P_X,\infty}^2 + \Vert w\Vert_{P_X,2}^2/n\right)$. If we only assume that $c\leq\hat{m}(x), \hat{g}(1,x) \leq 1-c$ in Assumption \ref{asmp:estimator-bounded}, then we would have the lower bound $\mathfrak{M}_{n,\gamma}^{\wate}\left(\gF_{e_n,e_n',f_n}\right) = \Omega\left( e_n' f_n\cdot\Vert w\Vert _{P_X,\infty}^2 + \Vert w\Vert_{P_X,2}^2/n\right)$. Furthermore, this lower bound still holds in the case where we know the baseline response, \emph{i.e.,} $\hat{g}(0,x)=g_0(0,x)=0$.

attestation.note: Verified against the authors’ arXiv:2402.14264 source archive (version dated 2025-06-10), sections/main_result.tex, Theorem 1 (label thm:ate) and Remark 2 (label remark:known-baseline). With e_n=r_0n^2, e_n'=r_1n^2, f_n=r_en^2 and constant w, square-root quantile risk is n^-1/2 plus max(r_0n,r_1n)r_en, equivalent up to constants to the stated sum; the paper’s following discussion states the lower bounds match the known DR upper bounds.

source.verbatim_statement: Given two arbitrary estimators $\widehat\omega(x)$ and $\widehat\mu(x)$, the class $\mathcal{P}(\epsilon_n,\delta_n)$ consists of all densities such that $\lVert\widehat\omega-\omega\rVert\leq\epsilon_n$ and $\lVert\widehat\mu-\mu\rVert\leq\delta_n$. Our first result is that the rate of convergence of any estimator of $\psi$ over this class cannot be faster than $n^{-1/2}+\epsilon_n\cdot\delta_n$.
